scheme_name: PMMSY: Establishment of large RAS / Biofloc culture system - Haryana
description:
The Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) is a flagship scheme launched by the Government of India on September 10, 2020. 

This scheme aims to bring about a significant transformation in the fisheries sector. 

It seeks to enhance fish production and productivity in the country. 

The PMMSY is particularly focused on promoting sustainable aquaculture practices. 

The scheme is designed to support the establishment of large Recirculatory Aquaculture Systems (RAS) and Biofloc culture systems. 

These systems are crucial for improving fish farming efficiency and sustainability. 

In Haryana, the PMMSY has specific objectives tailored to the state's unique aquaculture needs. 

One of the primary objectives is to increase fish production in Haryana from 1.5 lakh metric tons to 2.5 lakh metric tons by 2024. 

This represents an ambitious target of a 66.67 percent increase in fish production within a span of four years. 

The scheme also aims to create employment opportunities for around 15 lakh people in the fisheries sector by 2024. 

The PMMSY promotes the establishment of modern aquaculture practices. 

It encourages the adoption of technologies such as RAS and Biofloc systems. 

These technologies are designed to optimize water usage and reduce environmental impact. 

The benefits of the PMMSY include financial assistance for setting up aquaculture units. 

Under the scheme, financial assistance of up to 60 percent of the project cost is provided to beneficiaries. 

For SC/ST and women beneficiaries, this assistance can go up to 80 percent. 

The maximum financial assistance limit for RAS units is ₹2 crore per project. 

For Biofloc systems, the maximum limit is ₹50 lakh per project. 

The eligibility criteria for beneficiaries under the PMMSY are clearly defined. 

Applicants must be Indian citizens and at least 18 years old. 

There are no specific educational qualifications required to apply for the scheme. 

However, applicants must demonstrate a genuine interest in aquaculture. 

They must also have access to land or water bodies suitable for aquaculture. 

The income criteria for eligibility are not strictly defined. 

However, preference is given to small and marginal farmers, SC/ST, and women entrepreneurs. 

The application process for PMMSY involves several steps. 

Interested beneficiaries must first visit the official website of the Department of Fisheries, Government of India. 

They must download the application form available on the website. 

The completed application form must be submitted to the respective State Fisheries Department. 

Applicants must also provide necessary documents such as identity proof, address proof, and land ownership documents. 

A detailed project report outlining the proposed aquaculture system must also be submitted. 

Once the application is submitted, it will be reviewed by the State Fisheries Department. 

If approved, the applicant will receive a sanction letter detailing the financial assistance. 

The disbursement of funds is typically made in installments based on project milestones. 

The first installment is released upon approval of the project. 

Subsequent installments are disbursed after verifying the completion of specific project stages. 

The PMMSY is implemented by the Department of Fisheries under the Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying. 

The contact details for the Department of Fisheries can be found on the official website. 

The scheme is expected to contribute significantly to the overall growth of the fisheries sector in Haryana. 

It aims to promote sustainable fishing practices while ensuring food security. 

The PMMSY also emphasizes the importance of research and development in aquaculture. 

It encourages partnerships with research institutions to innovate and improve aquaculture practices. 

The scheme is aligned with the Government of India's vision of doubling farmers' income by 2022. 

It also supports the broader goals of the Atmanirbhar Bharat initiative. 

The PMMSY is expected to play a crucial role in enhancing the livelihoods of fish farmers. 

It aims to increase the availability of high-quality fish for consumers. 

The scheme is part of a larger effort to promote the blue economy in India. 

The blue economy refers to the sustainable use of ocean resources for economic growth. 

The PMMSY is expected to boost the overall economy of Haryana through increased fish production. 

The scheme also focuses on capacity building and skill development for fish farmers. 

Training programs will be organized to educate farmers about modern aquaculture techniques. 

This will ensure that beneficiaries are well-equipped to manage their aquaculture units effectively. 

The PMMSY also aims to improve the supply chain for fish products. 

This includes better marketing strategies and infrastructure development. 

The scheme encourages the establishment of fish markets and processing units. 

This will help in reducing post-harvest losses and increasing the income of fish farmers. 

The PMMSY is a crucial step towards achieving self-sufficiency in fish production. 

It aims to reduce India's dependence on fish imports. 

The scheme is expected to enhance the nutritional security of the population. 

It promotes the consumption of fish as a source of protein. 

The PMMSY is a comprehensive initiative that addresses various aspects of the fisheries sector. 

It aims to create a sustainable and profitable aquaculture industry in Haryana. 

The scheme is a testament to the Government of India's commitment to the welfare of fish farmers. 

It provides them with the necessary support to thrive in a competitive market. 

The PMMSY is a significant move towards modernizing the fisheries sector in India. 

It aligns with global trends in sustainable aquaculture practices. 

The scheme is expected to have a lasting impact on the livelihoods of millions of fish farmers. 

It represents a holistic approach to fisheries development in the country. 

The PMMSY is a vital component of India's strategy for sustainable development. 

It aims to ensure that the benefits of aquaculture reach the most vulnerable sections of society. 

This includes marginalized communities and those dependent on fishing for their livelihoods. 

The PMMSY is a forward-looking initiative that seeks to transform the fisheries landscape in India. 

It is a crucial step towards achieving the Sustainable Development Goals related to poverty alleviation and food security. 

The scheme is expected to pave the way for a prosperous future for the fisheries sector in Haryana and beyond.
